name: JioHotstar (formerly Disney+ Hotstar)
tagline: India's largest streamer: cricket, Disney/HBO content, regional shows, microdramas
facts: IPL, ICC (to 2027), HBO Max, Disney, Peacock

strategy.label: Mission
strategy.text: Bring every Indian premium sport and entertainment at a price as low as a cup of chai.

strategy.label: Vision
strategy.text: Be India's single default screen across mobile and connected TV, from cricket to microdrama.

strategy.label: Core strategy
strategy.text: Cricket as acquisition funnel; regional and global libraries retain; Jio telecom bundles convert free users to paid.

strategy.label: Moat
strategy.text: Near-monopoly on Indian cricket rights plus Jio distribution to ~500M telecom users and Star TV library.

strategy.label: Lesson
strategy.text: JioCinema's free IPL in 2023 forced the merger; free sports built reach but not profits, hence paywall return.

strategy.label: Your view
strategy.text: With cricket rights locked, is the real risk now regulatory (CCI dominance) or user fatigue with price hikes?

customers.pain: Need IPL and India matches live, cheaply, without lag
customers.why: Exclusive IPL and ICC streaming, multi-cam, regional commentary, ₹79 mobile entry

customers.pain: Paying for Netflix, Prime and others separately
customers.why: Disney, HBO Max, Star serials, live sports in one Premium plan

customers.pain: Little affordable content in own language
customers.why: Star regional channels, dubbed films, Tadka microdramas free with ads

customers.pain: Need mass reach beyond TV with targeting
customers.why: IPL scale (700M users), CTV growth, Jio data for targeting

customers.pain: Need sticky content to drive ARPU
customers.why: Bundled prepaid packs boost recharge value and retention

TV ads plus subscription fees; declining but cash-rich
Licensing content and sports rights abroad

bullets.label: Revenue mix
bullets.text: JioStar spans TV and digital; digital subs and ads growing while TV ad income softens.

bullets.label: Users vs payers
bullets.text: 530M MAU vs ~300M claimed paid peak; heavy non-paying, bundle-driven base.

bullets.label: Unit economics
bullets.text: IPL rights (₹48,390 cr cycle, shared TV/digital) need ads plus subs; low ARPU limits margins.

bullets.label: Growth levers
bullets.text: CTV upsell, price hikes, post-IPL retention via Tadka and serials, international licensing.

friction: Subscribers churn right after IPL ends
Frequent plan and price changes confuse users
Ads still shown on live sports in Premium
Device limits annoy shared family households
Clunky discovery across sports, serials and Tadka
